speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: asked	the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) whether the Ministry identifies and closely supervises cases of intellectually disabled persons who have no familial support or are estranged from their families; and (b) what can be done to prevent such vulnerable persons from being taken advantage of or abused.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Some may not have mental capacity or may lose mental capacity for decision-making and judgement.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Support for persons with disabilities, including those with intellectual disabilities, range from day care to long-term residential care.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The starting point is to see how they can best be supported within the family and within the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The wider community and public also have a crucial role to play in identifying and protecting these vulnerable individuals and to report any suspected violence or abuse.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In this regard, MSF launched last year a three-year "Break the Silence" campaign to encourage bystanders and members of the public who witness or suspect violence to take action and to report.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The campaign taps on social media, radio, television and roadshows to reach various segments in the community.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: For persons who lack the mental capacity to make specific decisions relating to their personal welfare or property and affairs, a Deputy may be appointed under the Mental Capacity Act (MCA) as a proxy decision maker for that person.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: One of the key roles of the Public Guardian is to supervise Deputies appointed by the Court for persons who lack mental capacity, which include those with intellectual disabilities.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The Public Guardian will also investigate whistleblower complaints on any alleged violation of the MCA provisions, including abuse or ill treatment of individuals without mental capacity, as well as instances of Deputies acting beyond the scope of the powers conferred on them by the Courts.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: If required, the Public Guardian will take appropriate action to safeguard such individuals, such as applying to the Courts to suspend or revoke an errant Deputy's appointment.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: In some situations, persons with intellectual disability, regardless of mental capacity, may be unable to protect themselves from abuse or neglect.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: The proposed legislation will allow the Government to protect individuals with physical and/or mental disabilities and who cannot protect themselves from abuse, neglect and self-neglect.

speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: This will complement existing laws that address violence, maltreatment and abuse against them.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo (Jalan Besar)
text: Could she have been put under Public Assistance scheme where she could have received more assistance and need not have to stay with the people who abused her?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: On the issue of register, we recognise that for persons with intellectual disability, it is a whole spectrum classified very, very broadly into "mild", "moderate" and "severe" intellectual disability.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Many young people who are diagnosed with intellectual disability get support when they are in preschool and when they go to SPED schools, whether they are in special needs education or in mainstream schools.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In that regard, agencies, schools, the community know who they are.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those with more severe needs, FSCs, specialised centres, preschools and schools will refer them, especially after they have graduated, to support services such as DACs.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For those with more severe needs, they will be referred to even institutional care, if required.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Caregivers are given the necessary support and grants to undertake training in order to better support family members with intellectual disability.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As for the horrific case of Ms Annie Ee, I would preface to say that it is a very sad case, which caught public attention and caused tremendous unhappiness at what happened to a young lady with intellectual disability who was out there, working and looking after herself.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The case had recently been up for sentencing and because there is an opportunity for appeal, I would like to preface by saying I would not talk specifically about the case.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, I will make general remarks about how as a community and as individuals and how as a network of Government agencies, FSCs and VWOs, we can work together to strengthen the support for persons with disabilities, including persons with intellectual disability.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In this particular instance, we are referring to a case of a person with intellectual disability who went out to work, went to find employment for herself, to look after herself.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The importance of having legislation to protect such persons cannot be further emphasised.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We have an existing set of laws in the Penal Code that allow us to take actions against abuses.

speaker: Dr Lily Neo
text: Am I not correct to say that there are about 4,800 Public Assistance recipients, which is about 0.1% of total resident population in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If she files a written Parliamentary Question (PQ), I would be happy to see whether the information can be provided.
